method: Qualitative whole-outline comparison using original source and baseline ordered coordinates, geographic placement, relative shape and coastal-map surroundings. No geometric registration, shoreline repair or name-boundary partition is claimed.

observations: The complete 26-position single ring occupies the mapped rounded waterbody immediately west of Lake Pontchartrain, with a broad southern curve, western side and narrower north/northeast outline consistent at regional scale.

The long eastern side remains within the western lake footprint and does not extend into the separately mapped Lake Pontchartrain. The southern and northwestern limits were considered as well as the label position.
Fine western indentation, small channels and exact shoreline vertices cannot be resolved on these regional maps; their absence from cartography is not treated as precise shoreline agreement.

The complete 41-position ring includes a broad southern body and a distinct northern lobe joined by a narrow middle section; neither the northern lobe nor southwest projection was omitted from review.
The readable Lake Salvador label on printed page18 is associated with the broad southern part. That label alone does not establish one uniform name over the whole inventory ring.

The acquired map silhouettes broadly correspond to the southern body, narrow middle and northern lobe, but the compressed cartography and project overlays do not resolve the northern lobe name, connecting-water name scope or a precise boundary between named waters.
The southwest projection and narrow coastal connections likewise require sufficiently detailed named cartography before a whole-feature identity or exhaustive constituent list can be completed.
records.assessment: The complete footprint was assessed on acquired cartography. The main southern label association is supported, while northern-lobe and connecting-water naming remain on a whole-feature scope hold.

coastal_context: The 2011 CELCP plan describes Lakes Maurepas, Pontchartrain and Borgne together as a shallow receiving basin affected by freshwater inflow and marine-water pathways. This supports a coastal/brackish basin context rather than an assumption of permanent uniform freshwater conditions.

For the Barataria basin, the same plan describes coastal marsh habitats ranging from fresh to saline conditions. This is regional context, not a salinity measurement or a water-class determination for every part of the Salvador-area polygon.
included_evidence_limit: The included files retain bibliographic references, own factual observations and selected public-domain geometry. Original publications and inspection materials are not included. Public offline validation checks included records and geometry; it does not reproduce visual map judgments.
